sources.title: 江阴银行2026年半年度报告
江阴银行2026年半年度报告摘要

thesis.core: Jiangyin Bank combines a sub-0.6x P/B valuation with low reported NPLs, very high provision coverage, solid core Tier-1 capital and a continuing cash payout. The valuation compensates for modest growth, NIM pressure and local-SME concentration, but rising watch/overdue loans and meaningful investment-income contribution keep confidence at medium rather than high.
thesis.normalized_earnings_basis: Value primarily on common P/B using 2026H1 attributable equity BVPS RMB7.50 and a 12-month forward/common BVPS reference around RMB7.70; use normalized EPS roughly RMB0.66-0.72 only as a cross-check because bank capital generation and credit cost dominate economics.
thesis.variant_wedge: The market appears to price persistent low ROE, NIM compression and eventual credit normalization. The variant view is that current asset-quality buffers and payout capacity are strong enough that even modestly stable ROE supports a P/B rerating and double-digit risk-adjusted return without requiring aggressive growth.

catalysts: NIM stabilizes around or above current levels as deposit costs reprice down.
Watch and overdue loan ratios stabilize without translating into higher NPL formation.
Interim/full-year cash payout remains sustainable while capital ratios stay comfortably above minima.
Provision coverage remains high while earnings growth continues without relying on outsized bond-realization gains.
kill_thesis: NPL ratio moves above roughly 1.0-1.1% with simultaneous watch/overdue deterioration and rising credit cost.
NIM falls materially below roughly 1.45% without offsetting funding-cost or fee-income improvement.
Core Tier-1 capital falls toward roughly 12.5% while loan growth remains aggressive or capital actions dilute common holders.
Recurring earnings become increasingly dependent on bond/investment gains while core spread and credit economics weaken.

normalized_earnings_basis.rationale: P/B is primary because sustainable ROE, credit cost, capital generation and payout dominate bank economics.
